title: Confirmed table navigation and handles
steps: Reset using Fixture checks. In A, press Tab from One and Shift-Tab from Four, then type: text must append at the destination cell end, without selecting its contents.
Enter in One/Two moves down the same column. Enter anywhere on the bottom row does nothing. Shift-Enter inserts a line break inside the cell.

In the final cell press Tab: it stays there and adds nothing. Use the bottom Add row and right Add column handles to append explicitly; verify B matches. Escape in a cell focuses the row handle for keyboard access.
expected: No row or column is created by Enter/Tab. Navigation changes only the caret; Shift-Enter changes only the current cell. Handles add one axis at a time through the shared authority. The old automatic-growth native trial was a superseded proposal, not this contract. Record physical chords and any unexpected selection/focus.

title: Cross-view undo and redo
steps: In A, paste abcd at the start of Alpha beta as one operation.
In B, paste FOREIGN between ab and cd as one operation. Return focus to A and use Command-Z, then Shift-Command-Z.
Also try ordinary typing and edits in different paragraphs.
expected: Origin candidate: undo leaves FOREIGNAlpha beta; redo restores abFOREIGNcdAlpha beta. Guarded step candidate may visibly refuse the unsafe batched inverse. Neither may silently delete B's text. These candidate outcomes are different; report what occurred.

title: Real IME composition
steps: Select a real Japanese, Chinese or Korean macOS input source. Compose a short phrase in a paragraph and an empty table cell.
Choose a candidate with Enter; separately start another composition and cancel it with Escape.
Try Shift/arrow candidate navigation and then type X. Write down input source and phrase in Notes. Repeat available languages; mark unavailable ones blocked in Notes.
expected: One committed phrase at the intended caret, no duplicate/dropped characters or unintended structural command. Cancel follows native behaviour. Final X enters the intended editor. Synthetic composition events do not count.

title: Native Edit menu and focus
steps: Edit in A, then B. Use the macOS Edit menu with the pointer to Undo/Redo in each focused view.
Try the keyboard shortcuts too. Open and dismiss a menu, then immediately type.
Switch to the other candidate window and back; verify the intentionally focused view receives commands.
expected: Menu and keyboard routes affect the focused editing context once, preserve the other view's edits, and return input to the intended caret. Disabled/unhandled menu commands are a failure or explicit blocker, not an automatic pass.

title: Native clipboard and selection
steps: Make a backward selection with the mouse, replace it, then undo.
Copy synthetic formatted text from TextEdit; use Edit > Paste and Paste and Match Style into a paragraph and a table cell.
Cut/paste plain synthetic text between A and B. Avoid task moves: their full lifecycle is not implemented in this comparison.
expected: The intended range changes once; plain-style paste strips formatting. Undo restores content without affecting another origin. Clipboard contents themselves are not read by the harness reporter.

title: VoiceOver and keyboard access
steps: Enable VoiceOver yourself with the macOS shortcut/settings. Navigate the fixture, table, toolbar and native checklist without the pointer.
Verify control names/state and a finite path into and out of the editor. Turn VoiceOver off when finished if desired.
Record any unnamed control, inaccessible operation or keyboard trap; mark blocked if VoiceOver cannot be tested.
expected: Core controls and editing paths are discoverable, named and operable. The harness does not enable VoiceOver or infer accessibility success.

title: Focus after formatting and view reopen
steps: Select text, format with the toolbar or Command-B, then immediately type.
Switch candidate windows during menu interaction; return to a chosen pane and type.
In the step candidate only, close and reopen view A while editing in B.
expected: No stale-range replacement or unwanted focus transfer. Reopened step view retains its context history. Candidate windows have independent authorities; this is not shared-document multi-window synchronization.

title: Save-failure protection (step candidate only)
steps: Enable Fail saves, type synthetic text, then use Protect & restart inside the page.
Verify text remains. Enable Fail recovery as well and try Close view A.
Verify close is blocked; turn both switches off afterwards.
expected: Accepted synthetic work survives in-page protected restart, or close refuses when neither path can protect it. This WKWebView uses an in-memory website store: quitting the native app is NOT an on-disk durability/crash-recovery test.
